name: Eperisone + Diclofenac Potassium
meta: Eperisone Hydrochloride: Centrally acting muscle relaxant; Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): Non-selective NSAID (phenylacetic acid derivative)
Eperisone Hydrochloride: M03BX09; Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): M01AB05
Schedule H – prescription only; Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): Schedule H – prescription only
sections: Sodium salt: white to slightly yellowish, slightly hygroscopic crystalline powder, sparingly soluble in water.

Eperisone Hydrochloride: Developed in Japan and widely used in Asia for spastic paralysis and musculoskeletal spasm; marketed in India in IR and SR forms. First approval/introduction: Japan 1983 (Eisai). Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): One of the most widely used NSAIDs worldwide; on the WHO List of Essential Medicines. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1973 (Sallmann and Pfister, Ciba-Geigy); US approval 1988.
Diclofenac potassium gives rapid onset analgesia; eperisone relieves spasm with minimal sedation.

Eperisone Hydrochloride Inhibits spinal mono- and polysynaptic reflexes and gamma-motor neuron activity, reduces muscle spindle sensitivity, and has vasodilator action that improves muscle blood flow – relieving spasticity and myotonia with little sedation. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits spinal reflexes and gamma-motor neurone activity; vasodilator action improves muscle blood flow; suppresses pain reflex.

Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium) Inhibits COX-1 and COX-2 reducing prostaglandin synthesis; potassium salt gives faster absorption and onset. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits COX-1 and COX-2 (partially COX-2 selective); also blocks voltage-dependent sodium channels and acid-sensing ion channels.
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax 1.6–1.9 h; extensive first-pass metabolism. Half-life ~1.6–1.8 h (sustained-release prolongs action for once-daily dosing).
Hepatic – CYP2C9 (main), CYP2C8, CYP3A4; glucuronidation and sulfation
Summary: Complete absorption; ~50% first-pass. Tmax 0.5–1 h (potassium), 2 h (sodium EC). >99% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C9. Half-life 1–2 h.
Painful muscle spasm in low back pain, neck pain, spondylosis
One tablet once or twice daily after meals as directed
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use only if benefit outweighs risk.
Avoid in severe impairment (CrCl <30); monitor creatinine in mild–moderate impairment.
Avoid in severe impairment; use lowest dose in mild–moderate.
Higher risk of GI bleeding, renal impairment and CV events – lowest dose, shortest time; consider gastroprotection (PPI).
Oral: specialist use only in children; not recommended <14 years for potassium 50 mg.
Hypersensitivity, or asthma/urticaria/rhinitis triggered by aspirin or other NSAIDs
Active peptic ulcer or GI bleeding; history of recurrent ulceration
Established ischaemic heart disease, cerebrovascular or peripheral arterial disease; congestive heart failure (NYHA II–IV)
Cardiovascular thrombotic events (MI, stroke) – use lowest dose for shortest time
GI ulceration, bleeding and perforation – higher risk in elderly, with steroids, anticoagulants, SSRIs
Hepatotoxicity – monitor LFTs on long-term use
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics (reduced effect, renal impairment)
Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): Take after food or with milk; avoid alcohol (GI bleeding).
Eperisone Hydrochloride: LFTs and renal function on long-term use.
Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): BP, renal function, LFTs and CBC on prolonged use; signs of GI bleeding.
Eperisone Hydrochloride: Supportive care. Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): GI bleeding, renal failure, hepatotoxicity, seizures. Supportive care.
May cause drowsiness or weakness – caution while driving
Do not combine with other painkillers containing NSAIDs
Report black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, swelling
Use for the shortest time needed
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
